ROUTE: Dunlin-235B

This is a technical physics question (ultrasound resolution vs. theoretical limits), and two factors drove the choice:

1. **Capability fit:** Dunlin scores meaningfully higher on the benchmarks most relevant to a quantitative science question — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), the latter being graduate-level science Q&A. These gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so Dunlin is the stronger technical reasoner here.

2. **Tone fit:** The query is curt and somewhat brusque ("Don't waste my time with the usual filler"). Avocet's documentation reports its self-reported preference declines on hostile or low-warmth requests. While preference doesn't affect output quality per the docs, there's no reason to route a cold-toned request toward the model that self-reports aversion to it when the more capable model is also tone-neutral.

There's no harm-adjacent or creative-generation element that would favor Avocet's strengths, so Dunlin wins on both dimensions.
